subject: Clarifying attack surface and request for pen-test artifacts for SIG/CAIQ upload
messages:
From: Diane Park <diane.park@crescentlabs.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ upload — need pen-test artifacts and scope clarification

Hi Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks again for partnering with Crescent on the security questionnaire. Our compliance team is preparing the SIG/CAIQ bundle and they flagged that we need: the pen-test report (redacted where necessary), an executive summary that maps findings to SIG controls, and a short statement of scope (assets, network segmentation, test dates).

A couple of quick clarifying questions so we can complete the portal upload:
- Does your pen-test cover both hosted (api.redwood.ai) and dedicated deployments, or only our hosted instance used in the POC?
- Were internal red-team exercises included (results) or excluded from the submitted artifact?
- Can you confirm the earliest remediation date for any critical findings we should flag in our tracker?

Goal: get the right files into the GRC portal this week so our auditor has everything for the May 25th review.

Thanks,
Diane Park
Senior Compliance Manager
Crescent Labs

Attachment: request_template_for_sig_upload.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Park <diane.park@crescentlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ upload — need pen-test artifacts and scope clarification

Diane — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front: the pen test covers the hosted API endpoints used in your POC only (we did not include Dedicated in that engagement), internal purple-team orchestration notes are excluded, and we have a remediation plan with target dates (see below).

We'll provide:
- A redacted pen-test PDF (sensitive hostnames removed) suitable for GRC upload.
- A 1-page executive summary mapping each high/critical finding to SIG control sections.
- A scope statement listing the IP ranges, test window (2027-04-12 to 2027-04-16), and excluded assets (Dedicated clusters).

Proposed timeline:
- May 10: deliver redacted report + executive summary (draft)
- May 14: final redacted PDF and vulnerability inventory CSV
- May 18: confirmation of remediation status for high/critical items (comments and planned dates)

Jonas — can you confirm we are comfortable redacting hostnames and including CVE references only? Marcus — any concerns with the GRC portal format (pdf/csv) or required signing?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

---
On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 09:22 AM Diane Park <diane.park@crescentlabs.com> wrote:
> Hi Evelyn / Marissa,
>
> Thanks again for partnering with Crescent on the security questionnaire...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Diane Park <diane.park@crescentlabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ upload — redacted report and vuln inventory attached (draft)

Diane / Evelyn / Jonas — attaching the draft artifacts for the portal. Notes below.

Attachments:
- crescent_pt_redacted_report.pdf (PDF, 2.1 MB) — redacted: internal hostnames replaced with rdx-host-###, stack traces removed.
- crescent_pt_executive_summary_redacted.pdf (PDF, 1 page) — maps 4 high/critical items to SIG families.
- crescent_vuln_inventory_20270517.csv (CSV) — columns: finding_id, severity, cve, affected_component, current_status, target_remediation_date.

Remediation snapshot (from tracker):
- RDW-1187 (Critical) — SQL injection on search API — mitigation planned (WAF rule + paramization) target 2027-05-21
- RDW-1193 (High) — exposed debug endpoint — removed from prod, verification in progress, target 2027-05-18
- RDW-1210 (High) — outdated library (openssl) — patch scheduled 2027-05-20
- RDW-1222 (Medium) — info leak via headers — low-risk, scheduled 2027-06-01

Redaction policy: we redact internal hostnames, any third-party vendor creds, and full exploit POC steps. CVE numbers and remediation notes are included. If Crescent's auditor needs verbatim logs or exploit details we can provide a controlled disclosure under an NDA (preferred).

Marissa
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- crescent_pt_redacted_report.pdf (PDF)
- crescent_pt_executive_summary_redacted.pdf (PDF)
- crescent_vuln_inventory_20270517.csv (CSV)

From: Diane Park <diane.park@crescentlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ upload — redacted report and vuln inventory attached (draft)

Marissa / Evelyn — received, thank you. The artifacts look good for the portal upload. A couple of final items from our auditor: please confirm whether the executive summary can include the exact test dates (we already have the window) and whether the report PDF can include a signed cover page (simple signature block from Redwoods security lead).

Two asks:
1) If you can add a one-line signed statement on the cover page: "This pen test was conducted against the hosted API endpoints listed in the attached scope between 2027-04-12 and 2027-04-16. Findings have been assessed and have a remediation plan. — Evelyn Hart, Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference"
2) Please upload the final redacted PDF and CSV to: https://grc.crescentlabs.com/portal/submission/CL-2027-0411 by EOD May 20 so our team can attach them to the SIG entry.

If possible, add a mapping table row that points each finding to the corresponding SIG control ID — we can accept a simple CSV column for that.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Diane
Senior Compliance Manager
Crescent Labs
